title: Interleaved warmup signal decay leads to hidden tenant throttles
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Summary: Several enterprise tenants reported intermittent token rejections and degraded throughput during a regional traffic surge despite metrics showing available reserved headroom. We traced this to a warmup accounting bug: when warmup tokens from multiple controller replicas interleave for the same tenant, a decay path can double-count a negative delta and drop the tenant below the canary/warmup floor. The tenant then silently falls back to burst-tier quotas and experiences throttles without an obvious spike in allocator utilization.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create two controller replicas (replica-A, replica-B) that both serve the same reserved pool for tenant 'acme-corp'.
2) Rapidly issue a mix of short-chat and embedding requests across two connection paths that land on alternate replicas (A/B) in sub-second intervals, reproducing interleaved warmup credit updates.

3) Observe warmup ledger for tenant: an instantaneous negative delta on one replica coincides with the other failing to apply its positive credit due to a racing cache invalidation, producing net warmup undercount.
4) Confirm that traffic is routed to burst-tier fallback and that per-tenant throttle counters increase while cluster-level headroom metrics remain stable.
5) Reproduce with a synthetic load generator in canary environment to validate fixes.

root_cause: Race in per-tenant warmup accounting when controller replicas apply local deltas to a cache-backed ledger. The local update path used non-idempotent subtraction for decay and relied on eventual reconciliation; when interleaved, a negative delta could be applied twice before the positive reconcile arrived, undercounting warmup tokens and triggering silent fallback to burst quotas.
mitigation: Hotfix (deployed to canary 2026-03-04): switch local warmup ledger updates to idempotent compare-and-swap semantics and add a short-term lock-free ordering token to reduce visible reconciliation windows.
Traffic-level mitigation: temporarily relax per-tenant burst fallback sensitivity for impacted tenants (account team opt-in) to avoid immediate SLA breaches while patch stabilizes.

Operational mitigation: instrumented a new warmup-gauge per-tenant in the Console with alerting when warmup delta variance > 15% over 60s and created a runbook for on-call to apply a manual bypass for VIP tenants.

Long-term fix: redesign warmup ledger to a single-source-of-truth service with leader-anchored updates or consensus-based commit path to avoid race windows across replicas. Scope and cost estimate below.
postmortem_actions: 1) Ship runtime-1.22 patch that enforces idempotent warmup updates and adds reconciliation backoff jitter (owner: infra-team).
2) Migrate warmup ledger to a lightweight leader/coordinator in runtime-1.23 (design doc + RFC draft linked).
3) Add e2e canary tests that simulate interleaved controller update patterns and assert no net negative warmup deltas under 1k/sec synthetic interleaving.
4) Update on-call runbook with new warmup-variance alert and explicit steps to escalate to infra-engineering and solutions engineering for customer comms.
5) Review reserved-pool fallback thresholds; add a tenant opt-out control for temporary bypass during escalations (product + legal review required).
6) Customer communications: send technical incident summary and mitigation timeline to affected customers; schedule postmortem sync with ACME and two other impacted customers.
